nodes.summary: Let $u$ and $v$ be linearly independent vectors in $\mathbb{R}^2$ and let $P$ be the parallelogram they span. The map $p \mapsto u + v - p$ is a bijection from the set of points of the triangle $\operatorname{conv}\{0, u, v\}$ that lie in the interior of $P$ onto the set of points of the triangle $\operatorname{conv}\{u, v, u + v\}$ that lie in the interior of $P$.
nodes.title: Point reflection between the two triangles of a parallelogram

nodes.summary: Let $u$ and $v$ be lattice points spanning a clean lattice parallelogram $P$ whose area is an integer $n \ge 2$. Then there is an integer $a$ with $1 \le a < n$ and $\gcd(a, n) = 1$ such that $P$ is unimodularly equivalent to the standard clean parallelogram $P_{a,n}$.
nodes.title: Clean parallelograms are unimodularly equivalent to standard ones

nodes.summary: Let $1 \le a < n$ be integers, let $n / a = [q_0; q_1, \dots, q_m]$ be the regular continued fraction of $n / a$, where $m$ is the least index at which it terminates, and let $v_j = (B_j, A_j)$ be its convergent vectors. Then for every natural number $i$ with $i + 2 \le m$, the determinant of the $3 \times 3$ matrix with rows $(1, B_{i-2}, A_{i-2})$, $(1, B_i, A_i)$ and $(1, B_{i+2}, A_{i+2})$ equals…
nodes.title: A determinant of three convergent vectors

nodes.summary: Let $1 \le a < n$ be coprime integers, let $n / a = [q_0; q_1, \dots, q_m]$ be the regular continued fraction of $n / a$, where $m$ is the least index at which it terminates, and let $v_j = (B_j, A_j)$ be its convergent vectors. For $p = (x, y) \in \mathbb{R}^2$ let $d(p) = |n x - a y| / \sqrt{n^2 + a^2}$ be the distance from $p$ to the line $y = (n / a) x$. Then: if $m \ge 1$, then…
nodes.title: Distances of the convergent vectors to the line $y = (n / a) x$

nodes.summary: For every rational number $x$, the convergent vectors of the regular continued fraction of $x$ begin with $v_{-2} = (1, 0)$, $v_{-1} = (0, 1)$ and $v_0 = (1, \lfloor x \rfloor)$, and its zeroth partial quotient is $q_0 = \lfloor x \rfloor$.
nodes.title: Initial convergent vectors

nodes.summary: Let $1 \le a < n$ be coprime integers, let $n / a = [q_0; q_1, \dots, q_m]$ be the regular continued fraction of $n / a$, where $m$ is the least index at which it terminates, and let $v_i$ be its convergent vectors. The lines $y = (n / a)(x - 1/2)$ and $y = n / 2$ cut the parallelogram $P_{a,n}$ with vertices $(0, 0)$, $(1, 0)$, $(a, n)$, $(a + 1, n)$ into four closed parallelograms: $P_1$ (lower left), spanned by…
nodes.title: Convergent vectors in the quarters of $P_{a,n}$

nodes.summary: Let $1 \le a < n$ be integers, let $n / a = [q_0; q_1, \dots, q_m]$ be the regular continued fraction of $n / a$, where $m$ is the least index at which it terminates, and let $v_i$ be its convergent vectors. For every integer $i$ with $-2 \le i < m$, the lattice points of the parallelogram spanned by $v_i$ and $v_{i+1}$ are exactly $0$, $v_i$, $v_{i+1}$ and $v_i + v_{i+1}$, and every point of $\mathbb{Z}^2$ equals…
nodes.title: Lattice points of the parallelogram of two consecutive convergent vectors

nodes.summary: Let $x$ be a rational number with regular continued fraction $[q_0; q_1, q_2, \dots]$ and convergent vectors $v_{-2}, v_{-1}, v_0, \dots$, and let $i \ge 0$. If the expansion of $x$ has a term $b$ in position $i + 2$ (it does not terminate before $q_{i+2}$), then $q_{i+2} = b$ and $v_{i+2} = v_i + b \, v_{i+1}$.
nodes.title: Recurrence for convergent vectors

nodes.summary: Let $1 \le a < n$ be integers, let $n / a = [q_0; q_1, \dots, q_m]$ be the regular continued fraction of $n / a$, where $m$ is the least index at which it terminates, and let $v_j$ be its convergent vectors. For every integer $i$ with $0 \le i \le m$, let $T_i$ be the closed triangle with vertices $0$, $v_{i-2}$ and $v_i$. Then the segment $[v_{i-2}, v_i]$ contains exactly $q_i + 1$ lattice points, the interior of…
nodes.title: Lattice points of the triangle with vertices $0$, $v_{i-2}$, $v_i$

nodes.summary: Let $x$ be a rational number with regular continued fraction $[q_0; q_1, q_2, \dots]$, and let $A_j$ and $B_j$ be the numerators and denominators of its convergents, given by $A_{-2} = 0$, $A_{-1} = 1$, $B_{-2} = 1$, $B_{-1} = 0$ and $A_j = q_j A_{j-1} + A_{j-2}$, $B_j = q_j B_{j-1} + B_{j-2}$ for $j \ge 0$. Stark's convergent vectors of $x$ are $v_j = (B_j, A_j)$ for $j \ge -2$, so $v_{-2} = (1, 0)$,…
nodes.title: Convergent vectors of a continued fraction

nodes.summary: Euclid's algorithm takes exactly one division step on $(2, 1)$, two division steps on $(3, 2)$ and five division steps on $(13, 8)$.
nodes.title: Euclid's algorithm on small inputs

nodes.summary: For natural numbers $u$ and $v$, the number of division steps of Euclid's algorithm on $(u, v)$ is $0$ if $v = 0$, and otherwise one more than the number of division steps on $(v, u \bmod v)$.
nodes.title: Number of steps of Euclid's algorithm

Write $A_i / B_i$ for its $i$-th convergent, and put $v_{-1} = (0, 1)$, $v_i = (B_i, A_i)$ for $i \ge 0$, $u_i = v_i + (1, 0)$ (so $u_{-1} = (1, 1)$) and $w = (a + 1, n)$. Then the vertices of the…
nodes.title: Vertices of the interior hull of a standard clean parallelogram

nodes.summary: Let $F_0 = 0$, $F_1 = 1$, $F_{k+2} = F_{k+1} + F_k$ be the Fibonacci numbers. Let $1 \le a < n$ with $\gcd(a, n) = 1$, let $P_{a,n} = \{s (1, 0) + t (a, n) : 0 \le s \le 1,\ 0 \le t \le 1\}$, and let $H$ be the convex hull of the lattice points in the interior of $P_{a,n}$. Then the lattice points on the boundary of $H$ are exactly the vertices of $H$ if and only if there is a natural number $k$ with $n = F_k$ and…
nodes.title: Clean interior hulls and Fibonacci numbers

nodes.summary: Let $1 \le a < n$ with $\gcd(a, n) = 1$, let $P_{a,n} = \{s (1, 0) + t (a, n) : 0 \le s \le 1,\ 0 \le t \le 1\}$, let $n / a = [q_0; q_1, \dots, q_m]$ be the regular continued fraction of $n / a$, and let $H$ be the convex hull of the lattice points in the interior of $P_{a,n}$. If $H$ has positive area, then $H$ has $2(m + 1)$ vertices when $q_0 > 1$ and $2m$ vertices otherwise (that is, when $q_0 = 1$), and…
nodes.title: Vertices and area of the interior hull of a standard clean parallelogram

nodes.summary: Let $1 \le a < n$ with $\gcd(a, n) = 1$, let $P_{a,n} = \{s (1, 0) + t (a, n) : 0 \le s \le 1,\ 0 \le t \le 1\}$, and write $\langle x \rangle = x - \lfloor x \rfloor$ for the fractional part of a real number $x$. The lattice points in the interior of $P_{a,n}$ are exactly the points $\langle k(n - a)/n \rangle \, (1, 0) + (k/n) \, (a, n)$ for $k = 1, \dots, n - 1$.
nodes.title: Interior lattice points of a standard clean parallelogram

nodes.summary: For points $u, v \in \mathbb{R}^2$, the parallelogram spanned by $u$ and $v$ is clean when $u$ and $v$ are lattice points and the lattice points on the boundary of the parallelogram are exactly $0$, $u$, $v$ and $u + v$.
nodes.title: Clean lattice parallelogram

nodes.summary: Let $F_0 = 0$, $F_1 = 1$, $F_{k+2} = F_{k+1} + F_k$ be the Fibonacci numbers, and let $N \ge 1$. Let $u > v > 0$ be natural numbers on which Euclid's algorithm takes exactly $N$ division steps, and suppose that $u \le u'$ whenever $u' > v' > 0$ are natural numbers on which it takes exactly $N$ division steps. Then $u = F_{N+2}$ and $v = F_{N+1}$.
nodes.title: Lamé's theorem (1844)

nodes.summary: For $u, v \in \mathbb{R}^2$, the parallelogram spanned by $u$ and $v$ is the set $\{s u + t v : 0 \le s \le 1,\ 0 \le t \le 1\}$.
nodes.title: Parallelogram spanned by two vectors

nodes.summary: The lattice points of $\mathbb{R}^2$ are the points $(a, b)$ with $a, b \in \mathbb{Z}$; they form the image of $\mathbb{Z}^2$ in $\mathbb{R}^2$.
nodes.title: The integer lattice in the plane

nodes.summary: Let $a$ and $n$ be natural numbers with $1 \le a < n$, and let $n/a = [q_0; q_1, \dots, q_m]$ be the regular continued fraction of $n/a$, where $q_0 = \lfloor n/a \rfloor$ and $m$ is the number of partial quotients after $q_0$ produced by the continued fraction algorithm (so $m = 0$ exactly when $a$ divides $n$). Then $q_m \ge 2$.
nodes.title: The last partial quotient of $n/a$ is at least $2$

nodes.summary: Let $x$ be a rational number. The continued fraction algorithm sets $x_0 = x$ and $q_0 = \lfloor x_0 \rfloor$ and, as long as $x_j$ is not an integer, $x_{j+1} = 1/(x_j - q_j)$ and $q_{j+1} = \lfloor x_{j+1} \rfloor$; it stops at the first index $m$ for which $x_m$ is an integer, so that $x = [q_0; q_1, \dots, q_m]$. For a natural number $i$, the $i$-th partial quotient of $x$ is $q_i$ when $i \le m$ and $0$ when…
nodes.title: Partial quotients of a rational number

nodes.summary: Let $a$ and $n$ be natural numbers with $1 \le a < n$ and $\gcd(a, n) = 1$, let $P_{a,n} \subseteq \mathbb{R}^2$ be the parallelogram with vertices $(0, 0)$, $(1, 0)$, $(a, n)$, $(a + 1, n)$, and let $S : \mathbb{R}^2 \to \mathbb{R}^2$ be $S(x, y) = (a + 1 - x, n - y)$. Then $S(P_{a,n}) = P_{a,n}$, and $S$ is an isometry of $\mathbb{R}^2$ for the maximum distance $d((x, y), (x', y')) = \max(|x - x'|, |y - y'|)$.
nodes.title: The point reflection symmetry of $P_{a,n}$

nodes.summary: For natural numbers $b$ and $n$ let $P_{b,n}$ be the parallelogram spanned by $(1, 0)$ and $(b, n)$, with vertices $(0, 0)$, $(1, 0)$, $(b, n)$, $(b + 1, n)$. Let $n$, $a$ and $a'$ be natural numbers with $n > 1$, $1 \le a < n$, $\gcd(a, n) = 1$, $1 \le a' < n$ and $a a' \equiv 1 \pmod{n}$. Then $P_{a,n}$ is unimodularly equivalent to each of $P_{n-a,n}$, $P_{a',n}$ and $P_{n-a',n}$.
nodes.title: Unimodular equivalences between the parallelograms $P_{b,n}$

nodes.summary: For natural numbers $a$ and $n$, the set $P_{a,n} \subseteq \mathbb{R}^2$ is the closed parallelogram spanned by $(1, 0)$ and $(a, n)$, that is, the set of points $s (1, 0) + t (a, n)$ with $0 \le s \le 1$ and $0 \le t \le 1$. For $n \ge 1$ it is the parallelogram with vertices $(0, 0)$, $(1, 0)$, $(a, n)$ and $(a + 1, n)$.
nodes.title: The parallelogram $P_{a,n}$

nodes.summary: Let $a$ and $n$ be natural numbers with $1 \le a < n$ and $\gcd(a, n) = 1$, let $P_{a,n}$ be the parallelogram with vertices $(0, 0)$, $(1, 0)$, $(a, n)$, $(a + 1, n)$, and for an integer $k$ let $S_k$ be the set of integers $y$ such that $(k, y)$ lies in the interior of $P_{a,n}$. If $a = 1$, the least element of $S_1$ is $1$ and the greatest is $n - 1$. If $a > 1$, then: for every integer $k$ with…
nodes.title: Lowest and highest interior lattice points of $P_{a,n}$ on each vertical line

nodes.summary: Let $a$ and $n$ be natural numbers with $1 \le a < n$ and $\gcd(a, n) = 1$, let $P_{a,n}$ be the parallelogram with vertices $(0, 0)$, $(1, 0)$, $(a, n)$, $(a + 1, n)$, and for an integer $k$ let $S_k$ be the set of integers $y$ such that $(k, y)$ lies in the interior of $P_{a,n}$. Let $k, l \ge 1$ be natural numbers with $k + l = a + 1$, and suppose that $y_L$ is the least element of $S_k$ and $y_H$ is the…
nodes.title: Lowest and highest interior lattice points of $P_{a,n}$ on paired vertical lines

nodes.summary: For natural numbers $a$ and $n$, let $P_{a,n}$ be the parallelogram spanned by $(1, 0)$ and $(a, n)$, with vertices $(0, 0)$, $(1, 0)$, $(a, n)$, $(a + 1, n)$. For an integer $k$, the set $S_k$ is the set of integers $y$ such that $(k, y)$ lies in the interior of $P_{a,n}$, that is, the $y$-coordinates of the lattice points in the interior of $P_{a,n}$ on the line $x = k$.
nodes.title: Interior lattice points of $P_{a,n}$ on a vertical line

nodes.summary: For a $2 \times 2$ integer matrix $M$ with entries $m_{ij}$ and an integer vector $u = (u_1, u_2) \in \mathbb{Z}^2$, the map $T_{M,u} : \mathbb{R}^2 \to \mathbb{R}^2$ is $T_{M,u}(x, y) = (m_{11} x + m_{12} y + u_1, m_{21} x + m_{22} y + u_2)$, that is, $p \mapsto M p + u$. It is an affine unimodular map when $\det M = \pm 1$; the definition itself puts no condition on $\det M$.
nodes.title: Integer affine maps of the plane

nodes.summary: Every subset $P$ of $\mathbb{R}^2$ is unimodularly equivalent to itself (take the identity matrix and the zero translation).
nodes.title: Unimodular equivalence is reflexive

nodes.summary: Two sets $P, Q \subseteq \mathbb{R}^2$ are unimodularly equivalent when some affine unimodular map sends $P$ onto $Q$: there are a $2 \times 2$ integer matrix $M$ with $\det M = 1$ or $\det M = -1$ and an integer vector $u \in \mathbb{Z}^2$ such that $\{M x + u : x \in P\} = Q$.
nodes.title: Unimodularly equivalent sets

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
